attempts.label: DANDI:001357
attempts.paper_title: High-Density Recording Reveals Sparse Clusters (But Not Columns) for Shape and Texture Encoding in Macaque V4
attempts.entry_title: Sparse clusters of shape and texture tuning in macaque V4 (Namima et al. 2025)
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Namima, Kempkes, Zamarashkina, Owen and Pasupathy (2025) on dandiset 001357, which holds the spike times of Neuropixels units from two monkeys in the shape, texture and position tests. It computes noise-corrected tuning similarity between simultaneously recorded neurons, its decline with distance along the probe (Isimilarity), contrast invariance, and the comparisons across penetrations, textures and stimulus positions. The LF signal, the stimulus images and the penetration coordinates are not in the dandiset.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Namima et al. (2025) from dandiset 001357

outcomes.statement: The shape test was run in 30 sessions in M1 and 44 in M2, the texture test in 17 and 34, and the position control in 33 M2 sessions; the responsiveness criterion excluded 461 and 366 neurons and left 1,850 neurons for shape and 979 for texture analyses.
outcomes.source: Materials and Methods, Dataset and data inclusion criteria, paragraphs 1 and 2
outcomes.quote: We conducted 30 and 44 sessions of the main shape test in M1 and M2, respectively. The position control experiment with shape stimuli was conducted in 33 of 44 sessions in M2 only. The texture test was conducted in 17 and 34 sessions in M1 and M2, respectively ... This excluded 461 and 366 neurons across our dataset for shape and texture analyses and left 1,850 and 979 neurons, respectively
outcomes.notes: The files hold 30 and 44 shape sessions (M1, M2), 17 and 34 texture sessions, and 34 position-test sessions (expected 33 within 3.3; one holds a single unit). 1,869 shape neurons are responsive and 427 excluded, 985 texture neurons responsive and 360 excluded, all within tolerance. The texture files' good units sum to the paper's 1,345 exactly; the shape files hold 2,296 against 2,311.
deviations: Texture responsiveness uses the original and contrast-reversed textures; the spectral-noise version in the files is left out, as the paper does not use it.
Shape responsiveness uses the dark (4 cd/m2) and bright (12 cd/m2) shapes; the files' third luminance level (8 cd/m2) is left out.

outcomes.statement: In penetration M2p6, 24 well-isolated neurons were recorded over about 2,400 um; a group of superficial neurons (1 to 9, over 540 um) had similar shape tuning at both contrasts, and with dark shapes neurons 1 to 9, 14 and 17 had a significant positive Isimilarity with a negative slope, while most other, deeper neurons did not.
outcomes.source: Results, Example penetration, paragraphs 1 and 2; Figures 2A, 3A and 3C
outcomes.quote: We recorded 24 well-isolated neurons in this session (Fig. 2A, left, #1-#24; superficial to deep) over a ∼2,400 μm length of the probe ... a small group of neurons (#1-#9) spread over a 540 μm extent of the probe in the superficial cortex (Fig. 2A, left) exhibited high similarity in their responses to the tested shapes ... For some neurons (Neurons #1-9, #14, and #17), regression lines were characterized by a large positive y-intercept (Isimilarity) significantly different from zero (p < 0.05, solid lines) and a negative slope (Ssimilarity)
outcomes.notes: The files' p06 of M2 (2021-04-14) has 24 responsive neurons spanning 2,340 um; neurons 1 to 9 lie over 540 um and are similarly tuned at both contrasts (mean similarity 0.70 dark, 0.86 bright, against -0.02 with deeper neurons). With dark shapes 13 neurons have a significant positive Isimilarity under both reliability readings, all with negative slopes; neurons 1 to 9 and 14 as in the paper, plus 12, 21 and 22, without 17. Count and set are outside the margin of one neuron. None has a significant negative intercept, so the two-sided count is also 13. With shared noise subtracted the count is 12, within tolerance, but the set lacks 17 and adds 12 and 21.
deviations: Penetrations are found by the files' `pen_ID` label (reading c of the claims file); readings a and b give other sessions whose counts do not match.

Depth is the unit's best-channel position from the files (20 um steps, `depth`, distance from the tip), measured from the most superficial good unit; the template center of mass of the Methods is not in the files.

The noise-corrected correlation was written from the Methods' description and Pospisil and Bair (2021) (Materials and Methods, Tuning similarity and contrast invariance); its bias terms are written for unequal repeats per stimulus (3 to 10 here), which reduce to the published terms with equal repeats. The paper's code is not public.

The bootstrap resamples each stimulus's repeats (500 times), with the same indices for all neurons of a session. Its distribution sits below the point estimate, since resampling with replacement inflates the noise the estimator corrects for, so the percentile interval is not a confidence interval of the corrected r; only its width decides reliability. Both readings of the reliability rule (width or half-width above 0.5) are run.

The noise of two simultaneously recorded neurons is taken as independent, as in Pospisil and Bair (2021). Their noise correlations are small but positive, largest within 100 um (mean 0.072); a variant subtracts each pair's noise covariance (`nc_corr_shared`).

outcomes.statement: The CSD shows a current sink taken as layer 4 at about 1,073 um below the most superficial neuron, 53 ms after stimulus onset, in M2p6, and at 570 um, 52 ms, in M1p12, with no other sink deeper in M1p12.
outcomes.source: Results, Example penetration, paragraph 1, and paragraph 4; Figures 2B and 4G
outcomes.quote: Current source density analysis (CSD, see Materials and Methods) reveals a current sink at ∼53 ms after stimulus onset at a recording depth of ∼1,073 μm relative to the most superficially recorded neuron in this session ... We found that a current sink with short latency (∼52 ms) emerged at a shallow depth along the penetration (570 of 2,580 μm, Fig. 4G), but no other sinks were evident deeper in the cortex
outcomes.notes: Needs the LF signal. The files hold spike times only; `acquisition` and `processing` are empty in all 159 files, and the archive's assets summary lists only Units and ElectrodeGroup. The paper names no other archive for the LF data.

outcomes.statement: In penetration M1p12, 42 neurons over 2,580 um showed no clustered shape tuning at either contrast; only one neuron had a significant Isimilarity, although most had high contrast invariance of shape tuning.
outcomes.source: Results, Example penetration, paragraph 4; Figures 4A, 4B, 4D and 4F
outcomes.quote: Here, we studied the responses of 42 neurons over a 2,580 μm distance (Fig. 4A) ... The y-intercept for the regression line was significantly different from zero for only one neuron (solid line) ... Neurons in this penetration did not exhibit shape tuning that was similar to their neighbors (filled), but most neurons did exhibit high shape tuning invariance
outcomes.notes: The files' p12 of M1 (2019-10-24) has 42 responsive neurons over 2,580 um, and 35 (a) or 36 (b) of 42 have reliable invariance above 0.5. With dark shapes the intercept's 95% interval excludes zero for 4 neurons under both reliability readings (1 positive, 3 negative). The claims file defines a significant intercept as one whose interval excludes zero, and the paper says 'significantly different from zero for only one neuron', so the count is 4, above the criterion's limit of 2; the partial rule needs the count to hold, so the outcome is not reproduced. Counting significant positive intercepts only gives 1, the paper's number. With bright shapes 5 neurons have a significant intercept (4 positive). With shared noise subtracted the dark counts are 1 positive and 4 of either sign. Changed from reproduced after verification round 1.

outcomes.statement: Of 1,850 neurons in 74 sessions (6 to 76 per penetration), a minority, 344 (203 in M1, 141 in M2), had a significantly positive Isimilarity with a negative Ssimilarity, reflecting similarity with nearby neurons that declined with distance; the majority (1,504) had an Isimilarity not significantly above zero.
outcomes.source: Results, Population results, shape tuning, paragraph 1; Figure 5A
outcomes.quote: We studied the responses of 1,850 neurons across 74 recording sessions (M1, 30; M2, 44), ranging from 6 to 76 neurons per penetration ... we found a minority of neurons (344/1,850; M1, 203; M2, 141; Fig. 5A, blue) with positive Isimilarity, significantly different from zero (p < 0.05), and a negative Ssimilarity ... The majority (n = 1,504) had Isimilarity that was not significantly greater than zero
outcomes.notes: Under all 12 readings a minority of the neurons with a line has a significantly positive Isimilarity (22% to 34%), nearly all with a negative slope, but no reading puts the four counts within tolerance. The closest, dark shapes, reliability (a), rule (ii), gives 394 (228 in M1, 166 in M2) and 1,335 not significant; bright (a)(ii) gives 381 (226, 155) and 1,349; dark (a)(i) gives 400 (233, 167) and 1,329. Penetrations hold 1 to 77 responsive neurons (6 within 0.6 fails); the single-neuron one is M2 p40 (2021-05-29), and the next smallest hold 6. Neurons with a line number 1,729 to 1,847 against the paper's 1,848. The criterion has no partial rule, so the outcome is not reproduced (changed from partially reproduced after verification round 1); the minority the statement describes holds. With shared noise subtracted the counts fall to 243 to 296 (M1 152 to 176, M2 91 to 121), also outside tolerance. The paper's 2 of 1,850 neurons without a line favour reliability reading (b) (64 here, dark) over (a) (140); a reader is asked (questions/001357.yaml).

outcomes.statement: Neurons within a penetration have slightly more similar shape tuning than neurons from different sessions (mean correlation 0.0582 against 0.0022), and more so within 200 um (0.0918 against 0.0435 further apart), but all means are weak.
outcomes.source: Results, Population results, shape tuning, paragraph 3
outcomes.quote: The mean of the correlation coefficient between the responses of neuron pairs recorded in different sessions was slightly but significantly less than that between simultaneously recorded neuron pairs (0.0022 vs 0.0582, respectively; Welch's t test, p < 0.0001) ... The mean correlation coefficient was even greater when it was based on neurons within a penetration separated by ≤200 μm (0.0918) than neurons that were further apart (0.0435; Welch's t test, p < 0.0001). Importantly, the means were quite weak in all three cases

statistics.about: different sessions against same session pairs
same-session pairs within 200 um against further apart

outcomes.notes: Under all 12 readings same-session pairs are more similar than different-session pairs and pairs within 200 um more than pairs further apart (Welch p below 1e-4). No reading matches all four means. Pearson's r of mean rates gives 0.0021 to 0.0036 across sessions, 0.0295 to 0.0317 within (0.0582), 0.073 to 0.074 within 200 um (0.0918) and 0.019 to 0.022 beyond (0.0435); the noise-corrected values are 0.006 to 0.009, 0.083 to 0.090, 0.195 and 0.056 to 0.066. All means are weak.
deviations: The noise-corrected correlation was written from the Methods' description and Pospisil and Bair (2021) (Materials and Methods, Tuning similarity and contrast invariance); its bias terms are written for unequal repeats per stimulus (3 to 10 here), which reduce to the published terms with equal repeats. The paper's code is not public.
The noise-corrected reading uses point estimates for all pairs so that same- and different-session pairs are treated alike; reliable same-session pairs are a variant.

outcomes.statement: Tuning similarity computed from orientation x spatial frequency fits (12 Gabor filters) to the shape responses is also diverse among nearby neurons, and its Isimilarity correlates with the Isimilarity from the shape responses (Spearman's r = 0.588, n = 1,848).
outcomes.source: Results, Tuning for stimulus orientation, paragraph 1; Figures 6A and 6B
outcomes.quote: Our results show that tuning preferences for orientation were quite diverse for nearby neurons, similar to our results based on shape responses (Fig. 6A). Across all penetrations, Isimilarity based on orientation × SF was strongly correlated with those based on shape responses
outcomes.notes: Needs the 120 shape images to compute Gabor filter outputs. The dandiset holds none (`stimulus/templates` is empty) and does not say which shape each stim_ID is. A search for a public, pinned copy of the Pasupathy and Connor (2001) shapes (the shape lab's publication pages, Pospisil et al. 2018 eLife, github.com/deanpospisil/er_est, the SparseShape OSF project) found none; other groups report obtaining them from the lab. A second search, in the final revision, found the outlines of the 370 shapes of the Pasupathy and Connor set at a pinned commit (github.com/deanpospisil/v4cnn, commit b0532e9083eb023c2247e5b53833229e7e6eb740, img_gen/PC3702001ShapeVerts.mat, 401 vertices per shape). The dataset still does not say which 15 of them the shape test used or which stim_ID each is, so the claim stays blocked here; using them needs the 15 shapes of Figure 1B identified in that set and a mapping of stim_ID to them, an analysis left to a new attempt.

outcomes.statement: Assayed at a coarse scale with two orthogonal orientations of the spindle shape, some penetrations consist entirely of neurons preferring horizontal or vertical, and in others the preference switches along the probe, as with optical imaging, even where single-neuron shape clustering is not extensive.
outcomes.source: Results, Tuning for stimulus orientation, paragraph 2; Figures 6C and 6D
outcomes.quote: We found penetrations that entirely consisted of neurons with preference for horizontal or vertical orientations (Fig. 6C) or penetrations where preference of neurons switched from one to the other (Fig. 6D), similar to what has been observed with optical imaging techniques
outcomes.notes: With stim_ID 0 as the spindle, 2 of 74 penetrations are all one preference and 2 switch once, so both kinds exist, but M2p6 (horizontal in bins 0 to 5, 0 to 599 um, vertical below, horizontal in its two deepest bins; 2 changes) and M1p5 (12 changes) are of neither kind. Under every stim_ID taken as the spindle, neither penetration is of one kind (M2p6 2 to 12 changes, M1p5 7 to 15), so the outcome does not rest on that mapping.
deviations: The files number shapes 0 to 14 without saying which is the spindle; stim_ID 0 is taken as Shape 1 of Figure 1B, and all 15 are shown.
Rotations 0 and 180 are taken as horizontal, 90 and 270 as vertical (Materials and Methods, Feature models).
Penetrations are found by the files' `pen_ID` label (reading c of the claims file); readings a and b give other sessions whose counts do not match.

outcomes.statement: Along angular position and curvature separately, clustering of tuning peaks is sparse; of 59 penetrations with at least four neurons well fit by the APC model, only 7 (angular position) and 5 (curvature) show a significant positive correlation between peak difference and distance, and only 9 and 5 sessions have smaller mean and STD of the differences than a permutation null.
outcomes.source: Results, Tuning for curvature or angular position, paragraph 1
outcomes.quote: Across 59 penetrations which included at least four neurons well-fit by the angular position × curvature model, only 7 (5) penetrations exhibited statistically significant positive correlation between the ΔAP (ΔCV) and inter-neuron distance (data not shown) ... we found that a minority (nine and five) of sessions exhibited smaller mean and STD than the null distributions (data not shown). These results indicate that evidence for clustered tuning ... is sparse in our dataset
outcomes.notes: Needs the boundary curvature and angular position descriptions of the shapes (Pasupathy and Connor 2001) and which stim_ID is which shape. Neither is in the dandiset. The shape outlines are public at a pinned commit (see orientation-sf-isimilarity), found in the final revision, but which stim_ID is which shape is not, and the analysis with them is left to a new attempt.

outcomes.statement: In M2p51, 33 neurons well fit by the APC model show mild clustering of angular position peaks (superficial neurons near 330 degrees, deeper ones near 180), with a significant positive correlation between delta AP and distance (r = 0.407) and none in that direction for curvature (r = -0.109).
outcomes.source: Results, Tuning for curvature or angular position, paragraph 1; Figure 7
outcomes.quote: The distribution of angular position peaks shows mild clustering with superficial neurons (magenta) tuned to features pointing to the lower right (∼330°) and deeper neurons (cyan) tuned to features pointing to the left (∼180°). This relationship can be visualized by the statistically significant positive correlation between inter-neuron distance and difference in angular position tuning peaks (ΔAP) for all pairs of neurons (Fig. 7B). No such relationship is evident along the curvature dimension (Fig. 7C)
outcomes.notes: Depends on apc-peaks-sparse-clustering, blocked for the same missing shape descriptions. The files' p51 of M2 (2021-06-11) has 48 shape-responsive neurons.

outcomes.statement: Restricted to the 18 M2 penetrations centered on the V4 gyrus, the percentage of neurons with significant Isimilarity is consistent with the whole population, also when only neurons within about 1,500 um of the most superficial neuron are kept.
outcomes.source: Results, Penetration trajectory, paragraph 1; Figure 8C
outcomes.quote: When we restricted our analyses to 18 penetrations centered on the V4 gyrus (Fig. 8B, rectangles), our results were consistent withwhat we observedacross the population (Fig. 8C, compare gray and black dots) ... clusters were sparse even when we restricted our analyses to the superficial cortex in those 18 penetrations, e.g., by considering neurons within ∼1,500 μm of the superficial neuron in each penetration
outcomes.notes: The 18 gyral penetrations are identified only by grid location and RF azimuth (Figure 8B). The files give neither the grid coordinates nor RF-mapping data; the electrode table's location is 'V4' for every channel.

outcomes.statement: For textures, of 979 neurons in 51 sessions (6 to 83 per penetration), a small subset (207; 18 in M1, 189 in M2) across 34 of 51 penetrations (7 in M1, 27 in M2) showed clustered selectivity, and 16 penetrations had five or more neurons with significant Isimilarity.
outcomes.source: Results, Population results, texture tuning, paragraph 1; Figure 9A
outcomes.quote: We studied the responses of 979 neurons across 51 sessions (M1, 17; M2, 34) ... (ranging from 6 to 83 per penetration). As with shape stimuli, we found that a small subset of neurons (207/ 979; M1, 18; M2, 189) across 34/51 (M1, 7; M2, 27) penetrations showed clustered selectivity ... Across the 51 penetrations, 16 penetrations had five or more neurons that exhibited regression lines with statistically significant intercepts (Fig. 9A, asterisks)
outcomes.notes: 985 texture neurons in 51 penetrations (6 to 83 each). No reading puts the counts within tolerance. Original and reversed textures under reliability (a) give 193 and 198 neurons (207) but 30 and 27 penetrations (34), 4 and 2 in M1 (7), and 12 and 7 M1 neurons (18). Reliability (b) gives 276 to 395 neurons in 37 to 42 penetrations. A minority of neurons with a line is clustered under every reading (27% to 41%). Neurons without a line are 304 and 322 under (a) and 62 and 44 under (b), against the paper's 48, which points to reading (b) for the paper's reliability rule. Five M1 texture files (2020-07-15, 07-19, 07-29, 07-30, 08-04) fail the clock check: 9% to 47% of their units fire more on stimuli than on blanks (median 41% across texture files) but 0% to 12% are selective among the textures, so their stimulus labels may not match the presentations. No neuron in them has a line under reliability (a) (original textures), so leaving them out leaves the (a) counts unchanged; under (b) it gives 267 to 379 neurons in 33 to 38 penetrations (7 to 11 in M1). No reading matches either way.
deviations: The noise-corrected correlation was written from the Methods' description and Pospisil and Bair (2021) (Materials and Methods, Tuning similarity and contrast invariance); its bias terms are written for unequal repeats per stimulus (3 to 10 here), which reduce to the published terms with equal repeats. The paper's code is not public.

The bootstrap resamples each stimulus's repeats (500 times), with the same indices for all neurons of a session. Its distribution sits below the point estimate, since resampling with replacement inflates the noise the estimator corrects for, so the percentile interval is not a confidence interval of the corrected r; only its width decides reliability. Both readings of the reliability rule (width or half-width above 0.5) are run.
Rotations are pooled per texture; the files do not store the rotation of each presentation.

outcomes.statement: Texture Isimilarity from original and contrast-reversed textures is consistent across neurons (Spearman's r = 0.464, n = 905).
outcomes.source: Results, Population results, texture tuning, paragraph 1; Figure 9B
outcomes.quote: Tuning similarity based on both sets of texture data (original and contrast-reversed) was highly consistent (Fig. 9B)
outcomes.notes: Spearman's r between original and reversed texture Isimilarity is 0.706 (reliability a, n = 624) and 0.642 (b, n = 894), p below 1e-90, against 0.464 within 0.0464. The neuron count under (b) is within 905 of 90.5. The consistency holds, more strongly than reported. Five M1 texture files (2020-07-15, 07-19, 07-29, 07-30, 08-04) fail the clock check: 9% to 47% of their units fire more on stimuli than on blanks (median 41% across texture files) but 0% to 12% are selective among the textures, so their stimulus labels may not match the presentations. Without them r is 0.706 (a, n = 624) and 0.675 (b, n = 834).
deviations: The noise-corrected correlation was written from the Methods' description and Pospisil and Bair (2021) (Materials and Methods, Tuning similarity and contrast invariance); its bias terms are written for unequal repeats per stimulus (3 to 10 here), which reduce to the published terms with equal repeats. The paper's code is not public.

The bootstrap resamples each stimulus's repeats (500 times), with the same indices for all neurons of a session. Its distribution sits below the point estimate, since resampling with replacement inflates the noise the estimator corrects for, so the percentile interval is not a confidence interval of the corrected r; only its width decides reliability. Both readings of the reliability rule (width or half-width above 0.5) are run.

outcomes.statement: For textures as for shapes, the fraction of neurons with a significant intercept levels off at about 20% when many neurons are recorded.
outcomes.source: Results, Population results, texture tuning, paragraph 1; Figure 10
outcomes.quote: Our results from texture (Fig. 10, black symbols) are consistent with those from shape (Fig. 10, gray symbols): the fraction of neurons with a significant intercept asymptote to ∼20% when the number of recorded neurons was large
outcomes.notes: Seven texture penetrations have more than 30 neurons; the percentage with significant Isimilarity is 25.6% to 52.1% pooled and 28.9% to 51.4% as a median under every reading, above 20 of 2. None of the seven is among the five M1 texture files that fail the clock check, and leaving those out changes no value (pooled 25.6% to 52.1%, median 28.9% to 51.4%).
deviations: The noise-corrected correlation was written from the Methods' description and Pospisil and Bair (2021) (Materials and Methods, Tuning similarity and contrast invariance); its bias terms are written for unequal repeats per stimulus (3 to 10 here), which reduce to the published terms with equal repeats. The paper's code is not public.

The bootstrap resamples each stimulus's repeats (500 times), with the same indices for all neurons of a session. Its distribution sits below the point estimate, since resampling with replacement inflates the noise the estimator corrects for, so the percentile interval is not a confidence interval of the corrected r; only its width decides reliability. Both readings of the reliability rule (width or half-width above 0.5) are run.

outcomes.statement: In 33 M2 penetrations (723 neurons), Isimilarity computed from responses at each neuron's optimal stimulus position correlates positively with Isimilarity at the aggregate RF center (r = 0.325), so stimulus position and RF scatter do not explain the sparse clusters.
outcomes.source: Results, Position invariance for shape tuning similarity, paragraph 1; Figure 12B
outcomes.quote: We found a statistically significant positive correlation between Isimilarity in the RF aggregate center versus RF optimal positions (r = 0.325, p < 0.0001, Fig. 12B). These results provide evidence against the possibility that stimulus position and RF variability contributed to the sparsity of clusters
outcomes.notes: 721 shape-responsive neurons in 33 M2 penetrations (723 in the paper) enter the position test (penetrations with 4 or more). Isimilarity at the optimal position against the main shape test with dark shapes (reading b) gives Spearman's r = 0.297 (reliability a, n = 378) and 0.325 (b, n = 676), p below 1e-4. Against the position test's center (reading a), r is 0.447 to 0.474 with the inferred center, p below 1e-4, so with the inferred center every reading gives a positive r with p below 0.0001 and reading (b) is within tolerance. Reading (b) does not use the position labels. Under reliability (b) the five choices of center give r = 0.274 to 0.406, all p below 1e-4, within tolerance only with position 3 (0.329); under (a) 0.279 to 0.567, p below 1e-4 except position 4 (r = 0.279, p = 2.1e-4), which fails the criterion's p below 0.0001. The outcome therefore assumes that the center is not position 4.
deviations: The files code positions 0 to 4 without saying which is the center; the position with the largest mean response of the penetration's responsive neurons is taken as the center (position 1 in 12 files, 2 in 11, 4 in 5, 0 in 3, 3 in 3), and all five are shown. The aggregate RF center is where the stimuli were placed on the neurons' RFs, so the population response should peak there; this is assumed, since the files do not label it. With position 4 as the center under reliability (a), p = 2.1e-4 and the claim would not be reproduced.
Neurons are those responsive in the main shape test; neurons responsive in the position test are a variant (603 neurons, r = 0.298 and 0.348).

Penetrations enter with 4 or more neurons, since a regression line needs 3 other neurons with reliable similarities (Materials and Methods, Clusters of similarly tuned neurons); this follows from the line rule.

outcomes.statement: In two example penetrations, the pattern of tuning similarity is the same at all five stimulus positions; a small cluster at every position in M2p9 and none at any position in M2p28.
outcomes.source: Results, Position invariance for shape tuning similarity, paragraph 1; Figures 11A and 11C
outcomes.quote: Results from two representative recording sessions are shown in Figure 11A,C, and in both cases, tuning similarity patterns were similar across all five positions
outcomes.notes: Under the criterion's rule M2p9 is the session whose responsive count is within 10% of 16, the files' p12 (2021-04-21, 16 neurons); there reading (a) fails for every choice of center and reading (b) finds 0 to 3 neurons with significant Isimilarity per position. Under reliability (a) this is not a test of p12, since only 0 or 1 of its 120 pairs is reliable at each position and no neuron has a line; under reliability (b) it has 13 to 39 reliable pairs. For M2p28 (the files' p28, 55 neurons) reading (b) fails, with up to 2 (reliability a) or 3 to 16 (b) such neurons per position against at most 1. Reading (a) fails for p28 under reliability (a), with position correlations from -0.06 to 1.00 and few reliable pairs (23 to 60 of 1,485), and holds under reliability (b) with position 0 as the center only. With the files' label p09 for M2p9 (18 neurons), reading (b) holds for M2p9 under both reliability readings, and reading (a) holds under reliability (b) for every center and under reliability (a) only with position 1 as the center. So with p09 as M2p9, position 0 as the center and reliability (b), reading (a) holds for both penetrations and reading (b) fails, which the criterion would call blocked; under every other choice both readings fail. Asked whether Figure 11's n is the matrix count, a reader answered that it is (16 and 55 sit with the matrices of panels A and C and Figure 12A; the RF insets read 8 and 26), so the claim and its 10% rule stand and the outcome is unchanged. On the data, the files' p28 has exactly 55 shape-responsive neurons (65 good, 44 responsive in the position test), consistent with matrices of shape-responsive neurons. No count of the files' p09 is within 10% of 16 (20 good, 18 shape-responsive, 12 position-responsive, 12 both, 18 either), so the rule still takes p12 as M2p9. Under that rule reading (b) fails on both p12 and p28 under both reliability readings, and reading (a) fails on p12 for every center under both, so the readings agree and the outcome is not reproduced, not blocked.
deviations: Positions are not labelled; reading (a) is evaluated for every choice of center.

The noise-corrected correlation was written from the Methods' description and Pospisil and Bair (2021) (Materials and Methods, Tuning similarity and contrast invariance); its bias terms are written for unequal repeats per stimulus (3 to 10 here), which reduce to the published terms with equal repeats. The paper's code is not public.

The bootstrap resamples each stimulus's repeats (500 times), with the same indices for all neurons of a session. Its distribution sits below the point estimate, since resampling with replacement inflates the noise the estimator corrects for, so the percentile interval is not a confidence interval of the corrected r; only its width decides reliability. Both readings of the reliability rule (width or half-width above 0.5) are run.

outcomes.statement: Simulated oblique penetrations through gradual tuning progressions in angular position and curvature give similarity matrices unlike the V4 data, while random tuning peaks interleaved with short stretches of similar tuning reproduce the observed localized clusters.
outcomes.source: Results, Simulation of tuning progression, paragraph 1; Figure 13
outcomes.quote: The resulting similarity matrices (Fig. 13A-C, bottom panels) were quite unlike our V4 data (compare with Figs. 3, 4). Random choice of tuning peaks in the APC space produced similarity matrices reminiscent of the majority of V4 data ... the observed patterns correspond best to random selectivity interspersed with small domains of similar tuning for shapes
outcomes.notes: A simulation judged by eye, with peak amplitudes and progression step sizes not given, which also needs the shapes' APC descriptions (not public, see apc-peaks-sparse-clustering). It uses no recorded data, so the dataset cannot test it.

findings.statement: The dandiset holds spike times of good units only. The LF signal behind the CSD analysis, the RF-mapping experiment, the stimulus images and the penetrations' grid coordinates are not in it, so the CSD, feature-model and gyral-penetration findings cannot be tested.

Shapes are coded by stim_ID 0 to 14 and the position test's positions 0 to 4 without saying which shape each code is or which position is the aggregate RF center. The position with the largest population response is position 1 in 12 files, 2 in 11, 4 in 5, 0 in 3 and 3 in 3, so the center cannot be read from the data either.
The trial tables of all 34 position-test files give the session as '...SL' (the shape test's code), while their units tables and file names give '...SP'.

The shape files hold a third luminance level, 8 cd/m2 (the background luminance), presented as often as the dark and bright shapes in 73 of 74 files; the paper and the dandiset description mention only dark and bright shapes. The texture files hold the spectral-noise version the description mentions and the paper does not use.

Unit depth is the best channel's distance from the tip in 20 um steps, not the template center of mass the Methods use; it gives the paper's distances for the example pairs (260 and 80 um) and spans (2,340 and 2,580 um).

The Methods say shape and texture tests were run in 34 M2 sessions; the dandiset has 34 M2 texture files of which 29 share a day and penetration label with a shape file, and 5 (p07, p17, p40, p42, p53) are texture-only days. The 2021-05-30 texture file is labelled p40, as is the 2021-05-29 shape file.

The position test has 34 files, where the paper reports 33 sessions; one (2021-05-29, p40) holds a single unit. The shape test of the same day is the penetration with one responsive neuron, where the paper reports at least 6 per penetration.
The texture files do not store the rotation of each presentation, which the Methods say was chosen at random from 8.

Spikes and presentations share a clock in 152 of 159 files (units are tuned to the stimuli at the photodiode onsets and not at onsets moved by -1.3 s). It could not be established in five M1 texture files (2020-07-15, 07-19, 07-29, 07-30, 08-04), where 0% to 12% of units are tuned at the true onsets, nor in the two single-unit files of 2021-05-29. In the five texture files 9% to 47% of units fire more on stimuli than on blanks (median 41% across texture files), so the units respond to stimulus onset but not selectively among the textures, which points to stimulus labels that do not match the presentations.

For the paper's authors. Is a noise-corrected similarity unreliable when the width of its 95% bootstrap interval exceeds 0.5, or its half-width, and what interval level is used? Under the width reading, 1,729 neurons have a regression line with dark shapes and 681 texture neurons with original textures; under the half-width reading 1,805 and 923; the paper has 1,848 and 931. The significant-Isimilarity counts change by 10% to 60% between them. How are unequal repeats per stimulus handled in the bias correction? And what does the estimator give when a neuron's bias-corrected variance is not positive? Here its similarities are undefined, and 62 of the 64 shape neurons without a line under the half-width reading lack one for that reason (the paper has 2).

For the paper's authors. Does the noise-corrected similarity between two simultaneously recorded neurons correct for their noise correlation? Here noise correlations are small but positive and largest for near pairs (mean 0.072 within 100 um, 0.023 beyond 800 um); subtracting them lowers the number of neurons with significant positive Isimilarity from 400 to 274 (dark shapes, width reading) against the paper's 344.

entries.name: 001357-namima-2025
entries.title: Sparse clusters of shape and texture tuning in macaque V4 (Namima et al. 2025)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Namima, Kempkes, Zamarashkina, Owen and Pasupathy (2025) on dandiset 001357, which holds the spike times of Neuropixels units from two monkeys in the shape, texture and position tests. It computes noise-corrected tuning similarity between simultaneously recorded neurons, its decline with distance along the probe (Isimilarity), contrast invariance, and the comparisons across penetrations, textures and stimulus positions. The LF signal, the stimulus images and the penetration coordinates are not in the dandiset.
